title: HB749 (2019 Regular): Firearms - Right to Purchase, Own, Possess, and Carry - Medical Cannabis (Patients' Rights Act)

other_topics: cannabis-policy: Section 1 § 5-701(G) — states the General Assembly's intent that medical cannabis be treated as legal under State law and patients not penalized for lawful use

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-701(B)): IN ACCORDANCE WITH § 13–3313(A) OF THE HEALTH – GENERAL ARTICLE, A PERSON MAY NOT BE DENIED THE RIGHT TO PURCHASE, OWN, POSSESS, OR CARRY A FIREARM UNDER THIS TITLE SOLELY ON THE BASIS THAT THE PERSON IS A QUALIFYING PATIENT.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-701(C)): A STATE AGENCY MAY NOT ACCESS A DATABASE CONTAINING THE IDENTITIES OF QUALIFYING PATIENTS TO OBTAIN INFORMATION FOR THE PURPOSE OF APPROVING OR DISAPPROVING A PERSON FROM PURCHASING, OWNING, POSSESSING, OR CARRYING A FIREARM.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-701(E)): A STATE AGENCY MAY NOT INQUIRE ABOUT A PERSON’S STATUS AS A QUALIFYING PATIENT FOR THE PURPOSE OF APPROVING OR DISAPPROVING THE PERSON FROM PURCHASING, OWNING, POSSESSING, OR CARRYING A FIREARM.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-701(F)): ANY FORM USED FOR THE PURPOSE OF APPROVING OR DISAPPROVING A PERSON FROM PURCHASING, OWNING, POSSESSING, OR CARRYING A FIREARM THAT INQUIRES ABOUT THE APPLICANT’S USE OF CONTROLLED DANGEROUS SUBSTANCES SHALL SPECIFICALLY AUTHORIZE A QUALIFYING PATIENT TO REFRAIN FROM REPORTING THE USE OF MEDICAL CANNABIS.
